canonical_question: Is the 'slight segregation' at 1023 K reversible upon cooling, or does it represent a permanent microstructural degradation that could nucleate voids under irradiation?

question_variants.question: Is the 'slight segregation' at 1023 K reversible upon cooling, or does it represent a permanent microstructural degradation that could nucleate voids under irradiation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence describes the formation of 'black spots' (segregation) above 1023 K during heating and their persistence/increase under irradiation. It does not address whether this segregation is reversible upon cooling or its specific role in void nucleation under irradiation.

answers.answer: The text states that above 1023 K, grains exhibited black spots indicating slight segregation. It notes that heating does not homogenously distribute compositional clustering and that the intensity of black spots increased with irradiation. There is no mention of cooling experiments to test reversibility, nor any discussion on the segregation's ability to nucleate voids.
answers.measurement_outcome: Black spots (segregation) observed; intensity increased with irradiation; no reversion observed.
answers.mechanism: Compositional clustering is not homogenously distributed after heating.
answers.boundary_limitation: No data on cooling reversibility or void nucleation mechanisms.
evidence_spans: A detailed characterization of the morphology and phase details of the as-deposited HEA films results in a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains with size in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm) and some regions of ultrafine grain sizes (100 to 500 nm) with an underlying single-phase BCC, with a lattice constant of ~3.2 Å
APT confirmed the EDS results, showing a film composition of 38% (±0.09) W, 36% (±0.09) Ta, 15% (±0.05) Cr, and 11% (±0.05) V.
The morphology is composed of very distinct compositional striations (layering) within the grains of ~4-nm thickness, which was not observed in EDS.
